patronOf.en-US: Patriarch of the monks of Palestine

prayerExcerpt.en-US: He was at first unwilling to consent, but finally founded a new monastery of persons all desirous to devote themselves to praise and serve God without interruption.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: A princípio relutou em consentir, mas finalmente fundou um novo mosteiro de pessoas todas desejosas de dedicar-se a louvar e servir a Deus sem interrupção.

meta.face: A Cappadocian Greek of about eighty-five, still upright, with a dry, sun-browned olive complexion and a TALL, OVAL face — a HIGH, ROUNDED forehead crossed by fine lines under THICK white hair brushed straight back to the nape (NOT bald), a LONG, straight nose with a sharply CHISELLED, slightly HOOKED tip, deep-set, keen grey eyes under high, ARCHED white brows, HOLLOW cheeks below clear cheekbones, a thin, firm mouth; a LONG white beard reaching the breast and DIVIDED at the end into TWO POINTS, as the Painter's Manual has him; the gaze searching and kind. Not the bald, broad, flat-faced theodosius_cenobiarch, his disciple john_silent (broad-templed, hump-nosed, eyes lowered), the convex-profiled, receding-chinned hilarion, the long, rectangular, furrow-browed john_climacus or the hooded, triangular anthony_abbot.
meta.basis: No likeness survives. The Painter's Manual of Dionysius of Fourna (`consult/hermeneia-ocr.txt`, line 7396, 5 December) gives him 'an old man with a beard divided into two points'; the age follows the book (he lived to ninety-four). The mantle, scroll and the laura of caves above the Cedron follow his icon on English Wikipedia and the book; the lion of his legend is left off.
